statement: For every such input, the function returns a result r, and r equals the maximum of the set of all k >= 1 for which there exist indices i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{k-1} with 0 <= i_t < len(arr) for every t and arr[i_{j+1}] = arr[i_j] + difference for every j with 0 <= j < k-1. Length 1 is included, with the adjacency condition vacuous.
preconditions: arr is a slice with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; -10000 <= difference <= 10000.

statement: For every such input, the function returns a result r; it does not fail (no overflow, out-of-bounds, or panic).
preconditions: arr is a slice with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; -10000 <= difference <= 10000.

statement: For every such input, the function returns a result r and there exists a strictly increasing sequence of indices i_0 < ... < i_{r-1} with 0 <= i_t < len(arr) for all t and arr[i_{j+1}] = arr[i_j] + difference for all j with 0 <= j < r-1. If r = 1 the adjacency condition is vacuous.
preconditions: arr is a slice with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; -10000 <= difference <= 10000.

statement: For every such input, the function returns a result r and for every k >= 1 and every strictly increasing sequence of indices i_0 < ... < i_{k-1} with 0 <= i_t < len(arr) for all t and arr[i_{j+1}] = arr[i_j] + difference for all j with 0 <= j < k-1, we have k <= r.
preconditions: arr is a slice with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; -10000 <= difference <= 10000.

statement: For every such input with difference = 0, the function returns a result r, and r = max { count(v) | v occurs in arr }, where count(v) is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(arr) and arr[i] = v. The set of occurring v is nonempty because len(arr) >= 1.
preconditions: arr is a slice with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; -10000 <= difference <= 10000; difference = 0.

statement: For every such input, the function returns a result r and the equivalence (r = len(arr)) if and only if (for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1, arr[i+1] = arr[i] + difference) holds.
preconditions: arr is a slice with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; -10000 <= difference <= 10000.

statement: For every such input, the function returns a result r and the equivalence (r = 1) if and only if (there do not exist indices i,j with 0 <= i < j < len(arr) and arr[j] = arr[i] + difference) holds.
preconditions: arr is a slice with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; -10000 <= difference <= 10000.

statement: For every such input, let rev be the slice of length len(arr) with rev[i] = arr[len(arr)-1-i]. The function returns a result r on (arr, difference) and a result r' on (rev, -difference), and r = r'.
preconditions: arr is a slice with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; -10000 <= difference <= 10000.

statement: For every such input and c, let arrc be the slice of length len(arr) with arrc[i] = arr[i] + c. The function returns a result r on (arr, difference) and a result r' on (arrc, difference), and r = r'.
preconditions: arr is a slice with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; -10000 <= difference <= 10000; let c be any integer such that -10000 <= arr[i] + c <= 10000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr).

statement: For every such input and k, let karr be the slice of length len(arr) with karr[i] = k*arr[i]. The function returns a result r on (arr, difference) and a result r' on (karr, k*difference), and r = r'.
preconditions: arr is a slice with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; -10000 <= difference <= 10000; let k be any integer with k >= 1 such that -10000 <= k*arr[i] <= 10000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr) and -10000 <= k*difference <= 10000.

statement: For every such input with difference != 0, the function returns a result r and r <= floor((maxVal - minVal) / |difference|) + 1, where minVal = min_{0 <= i < len(arr)} arr[i] and maxVal = max_{0 <= i < len(arr)} arr[i].
preconditions: arr is a slice with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; -10000 <= difference <= 10000; difference != 0.

statement: For every such input, let negarr be the slice of length len(arr) with negarr[i] = -arr[i]. The function returns a result r on (arr, difference) and a result r' on (negarr, -difference), and r = r'.
preconditions: arr is a slice with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; -10000 <= difference <= 10000.

statement: For every such input with difference != 0, the function returns a result r and r <= |{v | there exists i with 0 <= i < len(arr) and arr[i] = v}|, i.e., the number of distinct values occurring in arr.
preconditions: arr is a slice with 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -10000 <= arr[i] <= 10000; -10000 <= difference <= 10000; difference != 0.
